The direction holds and is solid in every round (c01 raw CPU AC 0.037-0.038 vs M100 0.100-0.102). Three problems: (a) the range for c01/c02/c07/c18 is 0.019-0.024; the 0.017 is c03's value. (b) 'Every single-lane cell' is wrong. In c04 (no host calls) M100 is +0.018 and AC +0.021. c11 is a four-way tie at 0.002, and c15 is AC = ABC = 0.044. (c) The mechanism is not adaptivity. C's window never opens in single-lane cells: win0 = 3201 of 3201 requests in c01/c02/c07/c18 (c14 82%, c15 99%), hot_iters = 0. So AC's gain there is just 'drop the 200 us busy poll, add 8 x 20 us deferral sleeps'. The claim should say this.

p90/p99 do match (about 106-110 / 118). Medians are not equal: M100 is lower by about 5-6 us in every round of c02 (63.0-64.0 vs AC 68.4-70.0), c07 (63.7-65.0 vs 65.9-69.2) and c18 (63.3-64.6 vs 69.2-70.0). They are equal in c09 and c14. Latency part is robust in every round. c01 > 1 ms: AC 0.97-1.12% vs M100 3.31-3.94% vs W 8.2-15.5%. c15: AC p99 119-128 vs M100 3,919-4,029 us. c15 load ratio is AC > M100 in all rounds. c01 load is weaker: round 1 is a tie (AC 0.979 vs M100 0.978), AC is ahead by 0.008-0.012 in rounds 2-4, and the min-max ranges overlap. Say '3 of 4 rounds'. No mechanism is stated or tested. A plausible one: under EEVDF, the 200 us busy poll costs the watcher scheduling credit (lag), so later wake-ups are not preempted. Test it with A and HOT_US=0.

Direction holds per round, but c10 has only 400 calls per run. The 1.69% vs 0.50% is about 27 vs 8 events in 1,600 calls, round 1 is a tie (0.75 vs 0.75), and A alone (0.19%) beats both, so C, not A, makes c10 worse (ABC 2.25% too). c17 is consistent (AC 28.6-32.7% vs M100 24.3-26.3% per round). c06: AC per-launch is 2,921-2,931 vs M100 2,877-2,904 in every round, so 12.4 vs 11.2 holds.

hot_iters / req is about 1,950 in c01/c02/c14/c18, i.e. about 200 us at roughly 100 ns per iteration. Raw CPU A 0.102-0.104 vs M100 0.100-0.102. Caveat 1: parks ~296 / park_timeouts ~293 appear in every no-gap no-load cell. They come from agent start-up (~300 ms of 1 ms backstops before the first launch), not from the loop. Real in-loop parking shows only in c09/c10/c11 and partly under on6 (c01: 634). Caveat 2: the us_* counters add integer-us deltas per ~100 ns iteration and undercount. Example: c18 A us_hot = 328 ms for 6.27M iterations (about 627 ms expected). Do not use them.

Medians match (AB/ABC 14.7-16.2, W 13.8-15.4) and the c17 numbers match. Four corrections. (a) c09 CPU is about 0.16-0.17 for both W and AB, not ~1.0. (b) Under on6 the gate is closed by loadavg (others >= 5 every check); latch_trips=1 is incidental. (c) 'Like A/AC' is false for ABC in bursts. With B on and the gate closed, C's hot window calls sleep_us(10) instead of cpu_relax. In c05, ABC has hot_iters 77k vs AC 4.0M, CPU 0.045 vs 0.114, and cost per call 21.6 vs 17.1 us. (d) AB is not free with the gate closed: > 1 ms AB vs A is 1.25-1.75% vs 0-0.5% in c10 and 4.0-4.4% vs 3.6-3.8% in c01, in every round. Likely cause: the 1 ms /proc preads (syscalls, i.e. preemption points).

Per round, AB is 1.34-1.88% and ABC 1.31-1.64% > 1 ms. The 1.70 is the minus-P value (raw 1.72). gate_opens medians are 1,248 (AB) and 966 (ABC), summed over 2 processes, so '1,000-1,250' is slightly high for ABC. latch_trips of 89/83 per run show the gate flapping. The > 1 ms values sit in the same 2.25-2.75 ms band as c13 (GPU time slice, see 11).

All 16 A-family c18 runs have unseen_latch=1 and unseen_hits=2. The two hits are the first timed graph launches (r1 A records 609 and 589 us); after that the runs are M100-like (median 69-70, p99 118). W is 531-537 us median in every round. W runs at the default 50 us timer slack (it never sets PR_SET_TIMERSLACK), which adds a little to its sleeps. The latch is fragile, though (see other findings #1).

The numbers are right, and the hypothesis is well supported by data already in hand. Every > 1 ms host call in c13 falls in one 2.25-2.75 ms band for every set (W/AB: 239 of 239 in 2.25-2.5 ms). The same band with the same share appears in c16 (on3) and as the main mode in c12 (on6), so it does not depend on CPU load. The share scales with the mean wait (W ~15 us gives 0.93%, sleeping sets ~70 us give 3.5-3.9%, ratio about 4). Better wording: a time-slice expiry that falls inside the wait gets charged to the host call (probability proportional to wait / slice). That is different from 'a late answer lets the other kernel run'. Also, p99 is fragile here because the tail share is near 1% (W 0.93% gives p99 373 us, sleeping 3.7% gives 2.5 ms); report the share instead. Cheap tests: (i) give the two processes different spins (2 vs 6 ms); the long-call band should follow the other context's slice or kernel. (ii) M100 with MAX_SLEEP_US 50/100/200; the > 1 ms share should scale linearly with the mean wait. (iii) P mode with the spin kernel recording its largest %globaltimer gap; ~2.4 ms gaps without bpftime would confirm the slicing. (iv) As root, change the nvgpu TSG timeslice and see whether the band moves.

Numbers confirmed: max 5,067-5,078 us, and P per-launch is 3,602-3,661 in every round vs 2,527 no-load and 2,577 under constant on6. The hypothesis is plausible. The > 1 ms values spread over 1-5 ms, get denser toward the end of the on-phase, and none go above ~5.1 ms. CONFIG_HZ=250 (4 ms tick) plus the EEVDF slice (~2-3 ms) means a wake-up that does not preempt waits for a tick-detected slice end, roughly until the phase ends. In-run signs of late wake-ups: AC guard_skips=1,192 and AB latch_trips=156 in c17. One gap: W's per-launch (3,072-3,298) is below P's in every round, so P is not a clean floor in c17. The hypothesis also has to explain why a WFE-spinning sibling thread helps the victim's main thread, which blocks in sync (P CPU 0.011). Cheap tests: a GPU-free thread doing 100 us clock_nanosleep and logging lateness under 'load2 6 x 5 5' vs 'load2 6'; vary the on-phase (2/5/10 ms) and see if the max follows it; 5 load threads or taskset to 5 cores; chrt -f or nice the watcher; perf sched timehist with /usr/lib/linux-tools/6.8.0-1020-nvidia-tegra/perf; as root, NO_RUN_TO_PARITY / NO_PLACE_LAG in sched features.

The c02 separation holds per round: sleeping sets 1,742-1,773 mW, WFE sets 1,691-1,745, P 1,685-1,703 (one overlap, ABC r3 1,745 vs AC r2 1,742). Two problems. (a) 'cpuidle WFI/c7 off' is inaccurate: state0 WFI shows disable=1, but its usage counter still rises (127 per second on idle cpu3 when checked today), because the menu governor falls back to state 0 when every state is disabled. Cores idle in WFI; only c7 is off. (b) 'Holds only under jetson_clocks' was never measured (no run without it). It is a scoping caveat, not a result.

P's window is 4000 x 324.6 us = 1.30 s, so P has no power value. It is worse than stated: only some runs have any power value. W 2/4, M100 1/4, A 2/4, AC 4/4, AB 3/4, ABC 1/4, each from about 9-10 samples (one second). So M100's 1,959 and ABC's 1,874 are single 1-second readings, and the medians in the table mix different numbers of runs.

other_findings: PATCH BUG (most important): the 'unseen' latch fires falsely on launches the hooks do note. 13 of 256 non-graph A-family runs have unseen_hits=1: r1 c02_AB, r1 c11_AB, r2 c11_AC, r2 c03_AB, r2 c06_AB, r2 c08_A, r2 c08_ABC, r2 c12_ABC, r2 c16_A, r2 c17_ABC, r4 c05_A, r4 c07_AB, r4 c10_A. unseen_hits is never reset, the threshold is 2 and the latch is permanent. In a longer-lived process, a second false hit would silently turn A/AC into M100-like behaviour with no parking (c11 CPU would go from 0.002 to ~0.011). Likely cause: note() runs after original() returns (a post-launch hook; the first note also calls cuEventCreate), and wait_for_note wakes only on notes, not on flag1. So a short probed kernel (the warm-up spins 1 us) can post its host call before its own note, and a backstop that expires in that gap counts as a hit. In c11/c02 the hit left no visible long latency, consistent with it being the warm-up record, which summarize drops. Fix: decay the counter or require consecutive hits. Test: a 10x longer c02, or many short probed kernels, while watching unseen_latch.

Attribution gap for C: the adaptive window is barely exercised. win0 is 100% of requests in every single-lane cell except c14 (82%) and c15 (99%); cap_forced = 0 everywhere; win300 is about 0 (2 events in c14 ABC). Every AC win in single-lane cells is 'no 200 us busy poll + 8 x 20 us deferral sleeps'. A control is missing: A with HOT_US=0 (and/or AC with K_DEFER=0). Without it the gain cannot be credited to C's grow/shrink logic.

Set definitions do not match the code for ABC. In the C hot path with B on, a closed gate gives sleep_us(P_MIN=10), not cpu_relax. So ABC vs AC is not 'AC plus WFE' in burst cells (c05: hot_iters 77k vs 4.0M, CPU 0.045 vs 0.114, cost per call 21.6 vs 17.1 us). Also ABC keeps C's deferral sleeps when the gate is open, which is why ABC CPU is about 0.93 vs AB about 1.0.

B has a cost under load even with the gate closed. AB vs A > 1 ms is 1.25-1.75% vs 0-0.5% in c10 and 4.0-4.4% vs 3.6-3.8% in c01, in every round (ABC vs AC in c10: 2.25 vs 1.69%). The only difference is gate_check's two preads every 1 ms. The latch counter mixes run_delay trips and late-WFE trips, which cannot be separated. WFE returns about every 100 us (wfe_waits about 27 per request in c02/c18, ~10.7k/s, i.e. the arm64 event stream), so LATE_WFE_US=500 fires only on preemption longer than 500 us. Also, loadavg's 4th field is an instantaneous count, and the open/close thresholds (>=5 closed, <=4 open) leave no hysteresis band; only OPEN_STREAK=3 damps it, so it flaps (c16: ~1,000 opens, 89 latch trips per run).

The rotation is only partly balanced. rounds.sh uses offsets r=1..4 out of 7, so each set gets only 4 of the 7 positions. P sits only in positions 3-6, always right after ABC (and right before W in r2-r4). AC sits only in 0-3; M100 in 0, 1, 5, 6; P/AB/ABC never run first. Each cell's first run follows the previous cell's last set (a different workload). With locked clocks and temps at or below 54 C the effect is probably small, but there are signs. c06 M100 per-launch is about 2,900 in r1/r2 (early positions) and about 2,877 in r3/r4 (late), the same order as some of the small claimed deltas. Use all 7 rotations, or randomise, before relying on deltas under ~1%.

Build fairness. diff -rq of the W worktree (46f5a7cb, clean) against policy/src over runtime/ and attach/ shows only bpf_attach_ctx_cuda.cpp differs, so the comparison is fair. Caveats: W's libbpftime-agent.so was built at 16:10, 12 minutes before commit 46f5a7cb (16:22), so the binary-to-commit match is assumed, not shown. And W never sets PR_SET_TIMERSLACK (default 50 us) while M100 and the A-family use 1 us. That matters where W sleeps (c18's 533 us, the c09/c10 gaps).

Statistics. Latency percentiles pool all runs and processes, so p99/max can come from a single run: c18 ABC r2 CPU 0.562 vs ~0.94 in other rounds; c13 ABC r3 p99 2,397 vs ~373 in other rounds; c16 W r4 p99 2,369. For bimodal tails (c13/c16) the > 1 ms share is the stable statistic and p99 is not. Report per-round ranges, or medians of per-run percentiles. Small-count cells (c10: 400 calls per run; c11: 1 call per run) need event counts, not percentages.

c17 baseline problem. P's per-launch (3,602-3,661) is above W's (3,072-3,298) in every round, so P is not a no-overhead floor there. The victim's main thread (device_flags 0x8, P CPU 0.011, so it blocks in sync) suffers the same wake-up delay, and per-launch or 'load vs P' comparisons in c17 are confounded by it.

The CLAIMS table never notes that idle parking happens mostly at start-up. parks ~296 / park_timeouts ~293 appear in every no-gap no-load cell, and the matching CPU and power are partly start-up (~300 ms before the first launch, outside the timed window for CPU but inside the process). The us_* counters are integer-microsecond sums per ~100 ns iteration, so they undercount by up to ~2x; flag this before anyone uses them.

Minor harness asymmetries: (a) non-P sets have the loader (syscall-server) process resident during the run, and P has none, which slightly affects load rate and power; (b) for loaded cells the load starts 1 s before the loader attach wait, so non-P victims start later into the load; (c) in c18 summarize keeps the graph warm-up latency record; (d) c14 power medians mix 1-4 runs per set.
